title: Ground Sample Distance (GSD)

GSD.description: Ground sample distance — ground dimension per pixel

applicability: Example: H=100m, pixel=3.3μm (1-inch sensor), f=8.8mm → GSD = 3.75 cm/px. For target GSD, solve for H: H = GSD×f/s_pixel.

title: Image Footprint on Ground
equation: W_ground = GSD × n_pixels_width;  L_ground = GSD × n_pixels_height
applicability: DJI Phantom 4 RTK: 5472×3648 px at 2.4cm GSD → 131 × 88 m per image. Used to calculate flight line spacing and trigger interval.

title: Flight Line Spacing (for desired sidelap)
applicability: 70% sidelap, 131 m width → 39 m line spacing. Similarly, trigger spacing along track: d_trigger = L_ground × (1 - endlap/100).

title: Photo Scale (vertical photography)
applicability: f=35mm, H=100m → S=1:2857. Scale varies across image with terrain relief: S_point = f/(H-h) where h = terrain elevation above reference.

title: Base-to-Height Ratio (Stereo Geometry)
applicability: B/H controls vertical precision. B/H = 0.3–0.6 is optimal for dense matching. Too low (B/H < 0.1): poor depth resolution. Too high (B/H > 1.0): matching failures. 80% overlap typically gives B/H ≈ 0.2–0.4 depending on geometry.

title: Vertical Accuracy from Stereo — Theoretical
applicability: Theoretical best-case. Practical accuracy 1.5–3× GSD with GCPs. Vertical accuracy always worse than horizontal due to stereo geometry. Convergent imaging improves vertical precision.

title: Reprojection Error (Bundle Adjustment Quality)

x_projected.description: 3D point reprojected through estimated camera model

applicability: RMSE < 0.5 px: excellent. 0.5–1.0: good. 1.0–2.0: acceptable. > 2.0: investigate issues (poor calibration, few matches, bad images). High reprojection error indicates geometric inconsistency in the solution.

title: GCP RMSE — Accuracy Assessment

RMSE_x,y,z.description: Component RMSE at check points (independent of control)

applicability: Compute on CHECK points (not used as GCPs in adjustment). Minimum 5 check points recommended (20+ for statistical rigor). Report separately for horizontal and vertical per ASPRS standards.

title: Image Blur Threshold — Maximum Shutter Speed

t_shutter.description: Maximum exposure time to limit blur to 1 pixel

applicability: GSD=2cm, speed=10 m/s → max shutter 1/500s. Mechanical shutter preferred over rolling shutter (which causes wobble distortion). Many mapping cameras now have global shutter or fast mechanical shutter.

title: Volume Calculation Error Estimate

n_pts_per_cell.description: Number of points per DEM cell

applicability: Simplified estimate. For stockpile volume: ±5–10% typical with 2–3 cm GSD and GCPs. Error proportional to surface area × height uncertainty. Systematic errors (datum offset) can dominate for cut/fill calculations — use check points on stable surfaces.
source: General practice, adapted from DEM error propagation
